gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 29?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 29 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data is unavailable or missing for the observation period, Weather Underground will be used as the secondary resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from sources like the German Weather Service and global ensembles point to a daytime maximum of 23–25°C in Munich on August 29 under clearing skies and light westerly flow following overnight showers. This aligns with the late-August climatological average high of 22.8°C while reflecting slightly warmer boundary-layer conditions from reduced cloud cover and downslope effects. Trader consensus, with 25°C holding 61.5% implied probability and 24°C at 33.5%, reflects model agreement on peak readings near the upper end of guidance, tempered by typical 1–2°C forecast spread and the possibility of localized cooling from residual moisture or timing of peak insolation. No major shifts in steering patterns or upper-level support have altered this outlook in the past 48 hours.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent cloud cover, widespread rain, and suppressed solar heating are positioning 27°C as the dominant outcome for Tokyo’s daily maximum on August 29.** Multiple forecast models and official guidance converge on a high near 25–26°C amid overcast skies, thunderstorms, and easterly to northeasterly winds that enhance mixing and limit boundary-layer warming. This represents a notable departure from late-August climatology, when clear conditions often allow peaks near 31°C.

Heavy precipitation (several sources project 10+ mm) promotes evaporative cooling and maintains high humidity, further capping temperature rise. With resolution imminent and little model disagreement on the overall pattern, traders have assigned 88% implied probability to 27°C while assigning only single-digit odds to 28°C or warmer. Minor upside revisions remain possible if rain clears earlier than expected, but current consensus strongly favors the lower end of the distribution.

This evidence-based positioning reflects aggregated trader assessment of official guidance and model consensus on a cooler, wetter day. This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 30 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast consensus from ECMWF, DWD, and ICON models points to a high-pressure ridge supporting mostly sunny to partly cloudy skies over Munich on August 30, yielding afternoon highs near 26–27°C—slightly above the late-August climatological average of 22.6°C. Light westerly winds and low humidity should limit mixing and cloud cover, while minimal precipitation risk keeps diurnal warming efficient. Ensemble spreads remain narrow given the short lead time, though minor shifts in ridge position or boundary-layer moisture could nudge the peak by 1°C. Updated model runs and official DWD briefings through the evening of August 29 will refine these probabilities ahead of market resolution.

This unsettled pattern aligns closely with the market’s near-even split between 20°C and 21°C outcomes, as traders weigh minor regional variations and potential forecast revisions from updated model cycles. Historical late-August averages in London hover around 21–23°C, underscoring how today’s suppressed thermodynamics favor the lower end of the distribution.

Light northerly flow and high humidity (often 70–90%) further suppress temperature rises, while isolated light showers or drizzle (15–30% probability) add evaporative cooling. Recent days have featured unseasonably cool, rainy conditions (highs near 24–26°C on the 29th), maintaining a stable, moist boundary layer that limits the typical late-August climb toward 30–31°C. 

The near-even market split between 27°C and 28°C reflects this narrow scientific uncertainty window, with small differences in cloud timing or wind shifts able to tip the daily maximum by a degree. Newer model runs or satellite observations of cloud trends over the next 12–24 hours remain the key variables that could shift the outcome.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 30 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent Met Office and European model guidance points to a maximum of 22–23 °C for London on 30 August 2026, directly supporting the market’s heaviest weighting on those two outcomes.** Southwesterly flow ahead of an approaching Atlantic front is expected to limit daytime warming while maintaining mild conditions, with widespread cloud and scattered showers or drizzle through the afternoon keeping surface temperatures from rising much higher.  

Forecasts show afternoon peaks near 21–23 °C under mostly cloudy skies and moderate southwest winds of 10–20 km/h, consistent with late-August climatology when unsettled patterns suppress extremes. Ensemble guidance shows low spread around this range, with only small upside risk if breaks of sun develop; downside risk is similarly limited absent stronger cold advection. Traders have therefore priced 23 °C as the modal outcome (49.5 %) and 22 °C as the next most likely (33 %), reflecting the tight consensus in official short-range forecasts issued 28–29 August. Updated model runs and the Met Office’s next public briefing remain the key near-term catalysts that could shift implied probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**High-pressure ridging over the Northeast is the dominant driver of trader positioning, supporting mostly sunny conditions and peak temperatures centered in the mid-80s at LaGuardia Airport on August 30.** Official National Weather Service guidance and ensemble model consensus project southwest winds of 5–10 mph with only a low (near-zero to 20%) chance of afternoon showers, favoring strong daytime heating while limiting moisture and instability.

The tight clustering between the 82–83°F (35.5%) and 84–85°F (29.5%) bins reflects genuine forecast uncertainty around secondary factors. Sea-breeze circulation off the Atlantic can introduce modest cooling if it strengthens in the afternoon, while variable cloud cover or slightly stronger winds would reduce solar insolation and lower the daily maximum. These elements create a narrow spread in maximum temperature guidance, with historical verification biases for urban stations slightly favoring the lower bin.

No major model disagreements or sudden pattern shifts have emerged in the latest runs, keeping probabilities closely balanced. The market-implied odds aggregate trader assessments of these subtle meteorological variables ahead of the final observation.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and ensemble models indicate a transition from persistent rain and cloud cover on August 29 to mostly cloudy conditions on the 30th, limiting daytime solar heating and keeping peak temperatures near seasonal norms for late August. High humidity from prior advection of moist air masses, light variable winds, and urban heat island effects in central Tokyo create narrow uncertainty around afternoon maxima, with numerical guidance diverging primarily on the timing and extent of any partial clearing. This scientific ambiguity—particularly between 26–28°C thresholds—explains the closely matched market-implied probabilities, as traders weigh model consensus against historical variability in post-frontal stabilization. Updated JMA guidance and next model runs expected overnight will likely refine the outcome ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Market-implied odds heavily favor a 22–23°C peak on August 30, consistent with official Met Office guidance and model consensus for London.**

The Met Office explicitly forecasts a daytime maximum of 23°C under bright or sunny intervals with isolated showers and southwesterly winds of 12–15 mph. Other numerical guidance, including ensembles, clusters tightly around 22–23°C as the most probable outcome, reflecting mild Atlantic air under a slack pressure gradient rather than the stronger anticyclonic setups that produced higher readings earlier in the summer.

Recent developments reinforce this positioning: persistent cloud and showers on August 29 have kept temperatures near or below seasonal norms (around 21°C), with the pattern evolving only modestly into Sunday. This yields limited diurnal warming potential and reduces the chance of outliers above 24°C. Historical climatology for late August at London Heathrow shows an average high of ~22°C, providing a baseline against which current model runs show only modest positive anomalies.

Traders appear to be pricing in the narrow uncertainty band typical of short-range UK forecasts, where small shifts in cloud cover or timing of any showers could nudge the verified maximum (from the London City Airport station) between 22°C and 23°C while keeping probabilities for 21°C or 24°C low. No major model divergences have emerged in the latest runs, supporting the current distribution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 30 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Traders see 29–30°C as the most probable range for Tokyo’s August 31 maximum because ensemble forecasts from global and regional models place the expected value near 29.5°C, with roughly equal chances of a modest positive or negative deviation. Persistent subtropical high pressure and southwesterly flow are maintaining warm, humid conditions typical of late-August climatology, while a weak frontal boundary and possible scattered convection introduce enough variability to split probability between 29°C and 30°C. The Japan Meteorological Agency’s guidance and medium-range ensembles currently show low risk of either a strong cool surge or extreme heat, keeping the 28°C and 31°C outcomes secondary but still viable within model spread. Updated model runs over the next 48 hours will be the key catalyst for any shift in market-implied odds.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 31 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest ensemble forecasts from the DWD, ECMWF, and GFS models indicate a maximum temperature of 23–25 °C in Munich on August 31, driven by moderate westerly flow, morning showers giving way to partial afternoon clearing, and surface pressures near 1018 hPa. These conditions align with climatological late-August norms (average high 22.4 °C) while limiting strong diurnal heating. Trader consensus reflected in the 44 % and 33.5 % implied probabilities for 25 °C and 24 °C respectively captures this narrow range, with residual uncertainty tied to the precise timing and coverage of convective activity that could shave 1–2 °C from peak readings.

Traders appear to weight verified station data from LaGuardia and Central Park heavily, with the slight edge to the lower bin reflecting typical urban verification biases. Updated NHC and local office guidance ahead of the weekend will be the next key input.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent cloud cover, widespread heavy rain, and moderate southwesterly winds are keeping London's peak temperatures suppressed on 29 August 2026, aligning trader consensus strongly with a daily maximum of 20–21 °C.**

Official guidance from the Met Office and cross-checked model runs forecast a daytime high of 21 °C, with temperatures climbing only to the 19–21 °C range amid overcast skies and frequent showers that limit insolation and enhance evaporative cooling. Current observations and short-range guidance show surface readings already hovering near 19–20 °C by midday under 90–100 % cloud cover and gusty conditions, reducing the likelihood of further warming. Historical climatology for late August in London places typical maxima around 19–21 °C, and the active frontal system today reinforces this cooler, wetter regime rather than any anomalous heat. 

Market-implied odds reflect this consensus: the 66 % probability on 20 °C and 28 % on 21 °C capture the narrow uncertainty band around official forecasts, while probabilities above 22 °C remain minimal (under 6 % combined) because additional warming would require unexpected clearing or stronger southerly flow not supported by current analyses. Minor upward revisions in afternoon model runs or localized urban heat effects could nudge outcomes slightly higher, but the dominant signal from precipitation and cloud persistence favors the 20–21 °C bracket.

Traders appear to weight verified station data from LaGuardia and Central Park heavily, with the slight edge to the lower bin reflecting typical urban verification biases. Updated NHC and local office guidance ahead of the weekend will be the next key input.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from multiple sources converge on a daytime high of 29–31°C for Tokyo on August 31, driven by increasing but still limited insolation under mostly cloudy skies, light easterly flow, and modest moisture that caps surface heating. Recent days featured persistent cloud cover and rainfall that suppressed maxima below seasonal norms, setting a baseline for only gradual warming as the pattern shifts. Ensemble guidance shows small spreads tied to the exact timing and coverage of any showers, which could shave 1–2°C off peaks if more persistent or allow brief spikes if breaks occur midday. This distribution underpins the tight clustering of market-implied odds around 29–31°C, reflecting both the narrow forecast envelope and inherent variability in late-summer boundary-layer conditions over the Kanto plain.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official National Weather Service forecasts for August 31 in New York City currently center on a daily maximum near 81–83°F under partly sunny skies with a modest 20% chance of showers.** Northwest winds around 5 mph and moderate humidity levels support this range, consistent with recent model runs from the National Weather Service that show limited day-to-day variability.

Recent observations reinforce the outlook: August 28–29 highs reached the low-to-mid 80s amid similar northerly flow and clearing conditions, while the August 30 forecast peaks slightly higher near 83–85°F before a modest cooling trend. Ensemble guidance and point forecasts (Central Park, LaGuardia, Kennedy) cluster tightly in the low 80s without strong signals for either a heat surge or sharper drop, though shower timing could trim the peak by a degree or two if clouds increase earlier than expected.

Trader positioning—led by 80–81°F at 36% implied probability, followed by 82–83°F at 23.5%—aligns closely with this consensus, reflecting the narrow uncertainty band typical for a short-range temperature market two days out. Historical late-August baselines for NYC further support outcomes in the upper 70s to mid-80s as the most probable band absent a significant pattern shift.

Key upcoming catalysts include the next 00Z–12Z model cycles and any rapid-update high-resolution guidance that could refine cloud cover or wind forecasts before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model consensus from the Japan Meteorological Agency and global ensembles shows Tokyo under increasing easterly flow with persistent cloud cover and light showers possible on August 31, limiting daytime heating and favoring a peak near 30 °C. This setup follows several cooler, rainier days that reduced surface heating and soil moisture, while subtropical high pressure remains positioned to prevent stronger subsidence and clearer skies that could push readings to 32 °C or higher. Relative humidity near 70 % during peak hours further caps the maximum by enhancing evaporative cooling. Traders assign the highest implied probability to 30 °C because ensemble spreads cluster tightly around this value, with only modest upside risk if afternoon clearing occurs. The next JMA forecast update and real-time surface observations on the 31st will provide the final resolution inputs.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent official forecasts from the National Weather Service and ensemble guidance position the highest temperature in NYC (LaGuardia station) on August 31, 2026, in the low 80s.** NWS tabular products issued August 29 project daytime highs of 81–83°F under partly cloudy skies with a 20–40% chance of showers and light northwest winds of 5 mph or less. This pattern favors modest surface heating without strong advection or clear-sky amplification.

**Key scientific drivers include a transitional post-frontal air mass with northwest flow suppressing extreme warmth, combined with limited moisture that caps afternoon dew points and convective development.** Historical analogs for late-August NYC under similar steering patterns show peak temperatures clustering near 80–83°F, with urban heat-island effects at LaGuardia adding slight upward bias relative to more rural sites. Current model consensus shows low spread, keeping probabilities concentrated in the 78–83°F bins and sharply discounting 84°F+ outcomes unless unexpected clearing or stronger southerly flow develops.

**Trader sentiment aligns with these data, as the market-implied odds closely track the NWS guidance and short-range model runs.** The 36.5% weighting on 80–81°F and 23.5% on 82–83°F reflect the most likely resolution window given stable conditions through the weekend. Any significant shift would require updated model runs or a revised NWS forecast showing stronger ridging or reduced cloud cover.

This places the peak well below the late-August climatological average high of ~81°F, consistent with cooler air advection following recent frontal activity. Afternoon readings have already stabilized near 78°F at key stations, with dew points in the upper 40s to low 50s limiting further warming. The market's 95.5% implied probability on the 78-79°F bin captures this tight scientific agreement, where surface observations, satellite data, and short-range models converge on modest daytime heating.

Realistic scenarios that could shift the outcome remain limited but include minor station-specific variances (e.g., LaGuardia Airport vs. Central Park) or unexpected boundary-layer mixing that adds 1–2°F. Stronger southerly flow or delayed cloud cover would be needed for a move into the low 80s, though current conditions and model consensus make this improbable before sunset.

Realistic scenarios that could shift the outcome remain limited but include minor station-specific variances (e.g., LaGuardia Airport vs. Central Park) or unexpected boundary-layer mixing that adds 1–2°F. Stronger southerly flow or delayed cloud cover would be needed for a move into the low 80s, though current conditions and model consensus make this improbable before sunset.
